model: Orbital Economy v7.7.11 Population candidate r1
note: Task 030 fragment. The 11 parameters declared by the population node are shared model parameters, not A/B copies. Model time is days; rates are fractions per model day. Values follow the population prototype and its calibration report; where the report defines a baseline rather than a fitted optimum, that is stated explicitly.

Population Birth Rate.role: Natural birth rate, 0.0000333333333333 per model day (1.2% per 360-day model year).
Population Birth Rate.effect: Multiplies each region's Population stock to form its Births inflow.

Population Base Death Rate.role: Baseline death rate, 0.0000277777777778 per model day (1.0% per 360-day model year).
Population Base Death Rate.effect: Multiplies Population and the living-standard mortality factor to form each region's Deaths outflow.

Death Living Standard Sensitivity.role: Dimensionless mortality elasticity to living standard, value 1.
Death Living Standard Sensitivity.effect: At value 1, mortality varies inversely with living standard, subject to the node's floor.
Death Living Standard Sensitivity.evidence: docs/research/POPULATION_PROTOTYPE_2026-10-04_RU.md: mortality × living-standard^-1; retained baseline, not separately fitted.

Labor Participation Share.role: Dimensionless share of population counted as labor force, value 0.50.
Labor Participation Share.effect: Labor Force = Population × Labor Participation Share for each region.

Migration Max Rate.role: Maximum migration outflow fraction, 0.0000555555555556 per model day (2.0% per 360-day model year).
Migration Max Rate.effect: Caps each directed migration flow before attractiveness-gap sensitivity is applied.
Migration Max Rate.evidence: docs/research/POPULATION_PROTOTYPE_2026-10-04_RU.md: no more than 2% of population per year; V7_7_11_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC §1.

Migration Gap Sensitivity.role: Dimensionless gain from normalized perceived-attractiveness gap to migration pressure, value 4.
Migration Gap Sensitivity.effect: Scales the positive attractiveness gap before the migration factor is capped at 1.
Migration Gap Sensitivity.evidence: docs/research/POPULATION_PROTOTYPE_2026-10-04_RU.md prototype migration setup; retained baseline coefficient, not separately fitted.

Attractiveness Perception Time.role: Perception smoothing time constant, 360 model days (one model year).
Attractiveness Perception Time.effect: Sets the adjustment time of Perceived Attractiveness toward current Attractiveness.
Attractiveness Perception Time.evidence: docs/research/POPULATION_PROTOTYPE_2026-10-04_RU.md: attractiveness perception smoothed over 1 year; V7_7_11_ARCHITECTURE_SPEC §1.

Attractiveness Wage Weight.role: Dimensionless exponent on normalized real wage in attractiveness, value 1.
Attractiveness Wage Weight.effect: Controls the contribution of Real Wage / Reference Real Wage to regional Attractiveness.
Attractiveness Wage Weight.evidence: docs/research/POPULATION_PROTOTYPE_2026-10-04_RU.md prototype attractiveness formula; unit baseline weight retained.

Attractiveness Jobs Weight.role: Dimensionless exponent on employment rate in attractiveness, value 1.
Attractiveness Jobs Weight.effect: Controls the contribution of Employment Rate to regional Attractiveness.
Attractiveness Jobs Weight.evidence: docs/research/POPULATION_PROTOTYPE_2026-10-04_RU.md prototype attractiveness formula; unit baseline weight retained.

Attractiveness Living Weight.role: Dimensionless exponent on living standard in attractiveness, value 1.
Attractiveness Living Weight.effect: Controls the contribution of Living Standard to regional Attractiveness.
Attractiveness Living Weight.evidence: docs/research/POPULATION_PROTOTYPE_2026-10-04_RU.md prototype attractiveness formula; unit baseline weight retained.

Reference Real Wage.role: Reference real-wage level, value 100 in model wage units after price-index normalization.
Reference Real Wage.effect: Normalizes Real Wage in the attractiveness formula so the wage term is dimensionless.
Reference Real Wage.evidence: docs/research/POPULATION_PROTOTYPE_2026-10-04_RU.md: reference real wage 100 was set manually; retained normalization baseline.
